sections.h2: Your options for a fast sale in Lynnwood
sections.html:
Lynnwood sellers have three routes: a standard agent listing, a for-sale-by-owner sale, and a cash sale to a buyer who takes the house as it is. A listing usually reaches the most buyers. A cash sale gives up some price in return for certainty and a shorter calendar, which helps if you are relocating, settling an estate, or carrying two mortgages.

Homes in Lynnwood are worth a lot compared with most of Washington. The median value of an owner-occupied home is $686,900, so even a small percentage gap between a retail price and a discounted offer adds up to real money. Before you decide, write down what each route would cost you:

  • Your mortgage payoff, plus any lien or home equity line.
  • Agent commission if you list, and the repairs a buyer is likely to ask for.
  • Real estate excise tax, which the seller usually pays.
  • Months of mortgage, tax, insurance and utility bills while the house waits for a buyer.

Compare the net figure from each route. A cash offer that looks lower on paper can land close to a listing once commissions, repair credits and holding costs come out.

Lynnwood is a growing, diverse city in southwest Snohomish County, about 16 miles north of Seattle where Interstate 5 meets Interstate 405. About half of households rent.

The even split between owners and renters means many Lynnwood houses, condos and townhomes have a rental history. A buyer who plans to keep a tenant will ask about the lease, so keep a copy ready.

Link light rail reached Lynnwood City Center station on August 30, 2024, giving nearby homes a direct line to Downtown Seattle and the airport. The station also works as a bus hub, and Community Transit runs two Swift lines, the Blue Line on State Route 99 and the Orange Line to Edmonds College, Alderwood and Mill Creek. Average travel time to work is 29.9 minutes.

If your house is a short trip from the station or a Swift stop, put the distance and the route in your listing or your pitch to a buyer. Houses farther away can lean on highway access, since State Routes 99 and 524 and both interstates serve the city.

sections.h2: Permits and what you can build
sections.html:
Many properties with a Lynnwood mailing address are outside city limits, so check your address on the city's verification map first. If you are inside the city, the Development and Business Services department issues permits through an online portal. The Permit Center is at 19100 44th Ave W and is open Monday through Friday from 8:30 a.m. to 4 p.m.

Some work needs no permit: fences under six feet, painting, playground equipment, and decks of 200 square feet or less. A typical remodel may need a structural permit, plus electrical, plumbing and mechanical permits when those systems change. Ask the Permit Center what is on file for your parcel, so you can answer a buyer's questions about past work.

An accessory dwelling unit can draw buyers. Attached and detached units are allowed in the Residential Neighborhood zone, up to 1,000 square feet, and each detached unit needs its own utility meters. The zone calls for a lot of at least 6,000 square feet, a 10 foot street setback and a 5 foot interior setback. Call the Planning Division at 425-670-5410 to confirm the current code before you promote a lot as ADU-ready.

Most sellers of improved residential property hand the buyer a seller disclosure statement under RCW 64.06.020. It is due five business days after both sides accept the contract, unless you agree to another time. The buyer then has three business days to rescind.

The real estate excise tax is the other big state item. It is usually the seller's cost and is payable to the county treasurer on the date of sale. The state schedule is graduated and a local add-on is included. For sales beginning January 1, 2027, the rates are 1.1 percent up to $551,000, 1.28 percent from $551,000 to $1,551,000, 2.75 percent from $1,551,000 to $3,051,000 and 3 percent above that. Earlier sales use thresholds of $525,000, $1,525,000 and $3,025,000. A sale at Lynnwood's median value lands in the second band.

Ask your title or escrow company to total the state and local amounts for your price before you accept an offer.

Snohomish County collects property tax in two payments, due April 30 and October 31. A mailed payment must be postmarked on or before the date. If the first half is not paid by April 30, the whole year's tax becomes delinquent, and charges are added on the first day of every month. Bills under $50 are due in full April 30. Interest on residential property with four or fewer units runs at 9 percent a year under RCW 84.56.020, with no penalties.

The county revalues property every year as of January 1, mails the notice in June, and uses that value for the next year's taxes. If you disagree, you can talk with an appraiser at the Assessor's Office. To appeal, file a completed petition with the Board of Equalization within 60 days of the notice mailing or by July 1, whichever comes later. The board's clerk is at 425-388-3407.

At closing, your escrow officer splits the current tax bill between you and the buyer.

Three providers serve Lynnwood: Snohomish County PUD for electricity, Puget Sound Energy for natural gas, and the Alderwood Water and Wastewater District for tap water. As your closing date nears, arrange final readings and account transfers with each one, and tell the buyer who supplies what so they can set up service on move-in day.

The order of events is similar whichever route you choose, though the timing is not.

  1. Gather your payoff figures, your latest tax statement and any permit records.
  2. Fill out the disclosure statement from what you actually know.
  3. Accept an offer in writing and deliver the disclosure within the five business day window.
  4. Let the title company order a settlement statement showing your payoff and the excise tax.
  5. Sign the deed, hand over the keys and arrange final utility readings.

With a listing, most of the calendar goes to showings, the buyer's inspection and loan approval. A cash sale skips the showings and the financing step, so the closing date is mostly up to you and the buyer.

sections.h2: What to ask a cash buyer
sections.html:
Get these items in writing before you agree to anything.

  • The exact price and the closing date.
  • Which closing costs each side pays.
  • Any contingency tied to inspection or financing.
  • A title company handling the closing, with a settlement statement showing your payoff and the excise tax.

Have an attorney read the contract before you sign. If the house is rented, ask how the buyer will handle the lease.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Lynnwood house as-is?
faqs.a: Yes, Washington allows as-is sales. You still must give the buyer the seller disclosure statement unless the buyer waives it or the transfer is exempt. Expect an as-is price to reflect the repairs the buyer takes on.

faqs.q: Does a house with a Lynnwood address always fall under Lynnwood permit rules?
faqs.a: No. Many properties with a Lynnwood address are outside city limits. Use the city's address verification map to see whether the city or the county handles permits for your parcel.

faqs.q: When do Snohomish County property taxes come due?
faqs.a: The first half or the full year is due April 30, and the second half is due October 31. A mailed payment is on time if it is postmarked by the due date. Missing the April date makes the entire year's tax delinquent.

faqs.q: How long do I have to appeal my assessed value in Lynnwood?
faqs.a: You have 60 days from the date the value notice was mailed or until July 1, whichever is later. File a completed petition with the Snohomish County Board of Equalization. The clerk's number is 425-388-3407.

faqs.q: Who pays the excise tax when a Lynnwood house sells?
faqs.a: The seller usually pays it. The buyer becomes responsible only if the seller does not pay. The tax is due to the county treasurer on the date of sale, so your closing agent normally deducts it from your proceeds.
